name: Start here
description: Reviews and the reports that set up the field.

item.title: Toy Models of Superposition
item.note: Small ReLU networks trained on sparse synthetic features keep more useful features than they have hidden dimensions; the reference point for the field.

item.title: Feature Superposition in Neural Networks: From Theory to Practice
item.note: Survey that organizes the theory by the class of decoder allowed to read features back, and the practice by the strength of the claims each result supports.

item.title: Open Problems in Mechanistic Interpretability
item.note: Open problems in mechanistic interpretability, covering methods and applications, including the limits of sparse dictionary learning.

item.title: A unifying framework from neural superposition to sparse interpretable codes
item.note: Connects superposition to identifiability theory, sparse coding through compressed sensing, and quantitative interpretability metrics.

item.title: Mechanistic Interpretability for AI Safety: A Review
item.note: Review of mechanistic interpretability methods for explaining internal representations and computations.

item.title: A Survey on Sparse Autoencoders: Interpreting the Internal Mechanisms of Large Language Models
item.note: Survey of sparse autoencoders: architectures, training, feature explanations, evaluation, and applications.

item.title: Toward Transparent AI: A Survey on Interpreting the Inner Structures of Deep Neural Networks
item.note: Survey of methods for interpreting the inner structures of deep networks.

name: Definitions and geometry
description: What superposition is, and how much overlap a given width forces.

item.title: From Data Statistics to Feature Geometry: How Correlations Shape Superposition
item.note: Defines superposition by overlapping directions plus recoverability, and shows that correlated features can be placed so that their interference helps rather than hurts.

item.title: The Linear Representation Hypothesis and the Geometry of Large Language Models
item.note: The linear representation hypothesis: a concept is carried by a direction and its intensity by the coefficient along that direction.

item.title: Lower Bounds on the Maximum Cross Correlation of Signals
item.note: The Welch bound: more unit vectors than dimensions force a minimum worst-case overlap.

item.title: Finite Normalized Tight Frames
item.note: Tight frames, which attain the lower bound on the total squared overlap of unit vectors.

item.title: Extensions of Lipschitz mappings into a Hilbert space
item.note: The Johnson-Lindenstrauss lemma: exponentially many nearly orthogonal directions fit in a given dimension.

item.title: Optimally sparse representation in general (nonorthogonal) dictionaries via ℓ¹ minimization
item.note: Exact sparse recovery from overcomplete dictionaries, the compressed-sensing side of superposition.

item.title: Emergence of simple-cell receptive field properties by learning a sparse code for natural images
item.note: Sparse coding of natural images, the origin of dictionary learning.

item.title: Linear Algebraic Structure of Word Senses, with Applications to Polysemy
item.note: Proves that a polysemous word embedding is approximately a frequency-weighted sum of sense vectors, which sparse coding recovers.

name: When training produces superposition
description: Conditions under which trained models share dimensions among features.

item.title: Polysemanticity and Capacity in Neural Networks
item.note: Defines feature capacity and shows that the loss-minimizing allocation shares dimensions among features of intermediate importance once feature values are heavier-tailed than a Gaussian.

item.title: What Causes Polysemanticity? An Alternative Origin Story of Mixed Selectivity from Incidental Causes
item.note: Incidental polysemanticity: networks with at least as many neurons as features can still become polysemantic.

item.title: Superposition Yields Robust Neural Scaling
item.note: Argues that loss falls as one over width in a strong-superposition regime, and relates this to loss-width fits on open language models.

item.title: Superposition Unifies Power-Law Training Dynamics
item.note: Derives power-law training dynamics from a superposition bottleneck in a teacher-student model.

item.title: Expand Neurons, Not Parameters
item.note: Splitting neurons into sparser sub-neurons at a fixed nonzero parameter count improves performance, attributed to fewer feature collisions.

name: Reading features back
description: How wide a layer must be for its features to be recovered, and by which decoder.

item.title: How Many Features Can a Language Model Store Under the Linear Representation Hypothesis?
item.note: One fixed linear map that reads back every k-sparse pattern needs a width of order k squared, up to logarithmic factors.

item.title: Stable signal recovery from incomplete and inaccurate measurements
item.note: Sparse optimization recovers every k-sparse signal from about k log(d/k) measurements under restricted isometry.

item.title: Taming Polysemanticity in LLMs: Provable Feature Recovery via Sparse Autoencoders
item.note: Feature-recovery guarantees for a sparse autoencoder variant under a generative model of activations.

item.title: Provably Extracting the Features from a General Superposition
item.note: Recovers the directions of a sum of ridge functions from noisy queries, under nondegeneracy conditions.

item.title: On the Limits of Sparse Autoencoders: A Theoretical Framework and Reweighted Remedy
item.note: Closed-form sparse autoencoder optima recover the true features only under stringent sparsity conditions.

item.title: A Unified Theory of Sparse Dictionary Learning in Mechanistic Interpretability: Piecewise Biconvexity and Spurious Minima
item.note: Casts SAE, transcoder, and crosscoder objectives as one piecewise biconvex problem; absorption and dead latents follow from the geometry of its solutions.

name: Computation in superposition
description: What a network can compute without first decompressing its features.

item.title: On the Complexity of Neural Computation in Superposition
item.note: Storing sparse Boolean features takes logarithmic width, while computing a whole family of such functions needs more width than storing their outputs.

item.title: Mathematical Models of Computation in Superposition
item.note: Constructions that compute all pairwise ANDs of sparse features in superposition; even random networks make many such functions linearly readable.

item.title: Towards Combinatorial Interpretability of Neural Computation
item.note: Reads output-channel routing motifs off the weight signs of two-layer MLPs trained on sparse Boolean formulas.

item.title: Compressed Computation is (probably) not Computation in Superposition
item.note: Shows that a reported loss advantage for compressed computation comes from a linear mixing term created by the residual and the embedding.

item.title: Compressed Computation under L⁴ Loss is likely Computation in Superposition
item.note: Removes the residual and trains under a fourth-power loss, which yields a sparse code consistent with computation in superposition.

item.title: Temporal Superposition and Feature Geometry of RNNs under Memory Demands
item.note: Superposition across time in recurrent networks, with an exact loss decomposition into projection and composition interference.

name: Superposition as an explanation
description: Phenomena that superposition has been proposed to explain.

item.title: Adversarial Examples Are Not Bugs, They Are Superposition
item.note: Argues that superposition may be a primary cause of adversarial examples.

item.title: Adversarial Attacks Leverage Interference Between Features in Superposition
item.note: Proves that optimal perturbations in a linear bottleneck follow the interference between readout directions.

item.title: Superposition as Lossy Compression: Measure with Sparse Autoencoders and Connect to Adversarial Vulnerability
item.note: Counts effective features per neuron with an entropy measure built on sparse autoencoders, and relates the count to adversarial training.

item.title: Similarity of Neural Network Representations in Superposition
item.note: How RSA, linear CKA, and linear regression behave on representations in superposition.

item.title: The importance of mixed selectivity in complex cognitive tasks
item.note: Neuroscience: nonlinear mixed selectivity raises the dimension of neural activity and supports linear classification.

item.title: Neural Population Coding of Multiple Stimuli
item.note: Neuroscience: decoding several stimuli from one neural population with unbiased and optimal linear estimators.

name: Supervised probes
description: Reading a property named in advance from the activations.

item.title: Finding Neurons in a Haystack: Case Studies with Sparse Probing
item.note: Sparse probing: restricts a probe to a few neurons to test whether a property is localized in the neuron basis.

item.title: Towards Principled Evaluations of Sparse Autoencoders for Interpretability and Control
item.note: Supervised dictionaries built from class-conditional means, used as a reference against which sparse autoencoders are tested causally.

name: Sparse autoencoders
description: Unsupervised dictionaries that estimate features from activations.

item.title: Towards Monosemanticity: Decomposing Language Models With Dictionary Learning
item.note: Dictionary learning on a one-layer transformer, decomposing polysemantic neurons into sparse latents.

item.title: Sparse Autoencoders Find Highly Interpretable Features in Language Models
item.note: Trains sparse autoencoders on language-model activations to find interpretable directions.

item.title: Scaling Monosemanticity: Extracting Interpretable Features from Claude 3 Sonnet
item.note: Scales sparse autoencoders to a production model, with up to 34 million latents on Claude 3 Sonnet.

item.title: Scaling and Evaluating Sparse Autoencoders
item.note: TopK sparse autoencoders with an auxiliary loss against dead latents, scaled to 16 million latents on GPT-4 activations.

item.title: Improving Dictionary Learning with Gated Sparse Autoencoders
item.note: Separates which latents fire from how large they are, removing the shrinkage caused by the L1 penalty.

item.title: Jumping Ahead: Improving Reconstruction Fidelity with JumpReLU Sparse Autoencoders
item.note: Per-latent thresholds that allow variable activity without coupling latents to each other.

item.title: BatchTopK Sparse Autoencoders
item.note: Selects the active latents per batch instead of per example.

item.title: Learning Multi-Level Features with Matryoshka Sparse Autoencoders
item.note: Nested dictionaries that change how related properties share latents, reducing absorption as width grows.

item.title: Identifying Functionally Important Features with End-to-End Sparse Dictionary Learning
item.note: Trains the dictionary on the model's downstream loss instead of activation reconstruction.

item.title: Gemma Scope: Open Sparse Autoencoders Everywhere All at Once on Gemma 2
item.note: More than 400 open sparse autoencoders across every layer of Gemma 2 2B and 9B, plus selected layers of 27B.

name: Transcoders, crosscoders, and circuits
description: Interpretable stand-ins for parts of the network's computation.

item.title: Transcoders Find Interpretable LLM Feature Circuits
item.note: Replaces MLPs with sparse transcoders, so that latent-to-latent attributions factorize through the weights.

item.title: Sparse Feature Circuits: Discovering and Editing Interpretable Causal Graphs in Language Models
item.note: Builds circuits from sparse autoencoder latents with error nodes, and edits model behavior through them.

item.title: Sparse Crosscoders for Cross-Layer Features and Model Diffing
item.note: Latents that read from and write to several layers, also used to compare two models.

item.title: Circuit Tracing: Revealing Computational Graphs in Language Models
item.note: Cross-layer transcoders and attribution graphs for tracing a model's computation on a prompt.

item.title: On the Biology of a Large Language Model
item.note: Attribution graphs applied to many behaviors of Claude 3.5 Haiku; the authors report insight on about a quarter of the prompts they tried.

item.title: Sparse Mixtures of Linear Transforms
item.note: Replacement layers built from sparse mixtures of linear transforms.

item.title: Insights on Crosscoder Model Diffing
item.note: How the crosscoder objective decides which latents are exclusive to one of two models.

name: Parameter decomposition
description: Decomposing the trained weights into mechanisms.

item.title: A Toy Model of Interference Weights
item.note: Argues that superposition contaminates the weights between features, motivating decomposition in parameter space.

item.title: Interpretability in Parameter Space: Minimizing Mechanistic Description Length with Attribution-based Parameter Decomposition
item.note: Decomposes weights into mechanisms by minimizing description length; recovers ground-truth mechanisms in toy models.

item.title: Stochastic Parameter Decomposition
item.note: A stochastic, more scalable form of parameter decomposition.

item.title: Interpreting Language Model Parameters
item.note: Extends parameter decomposition to language models and tests components with adversarially chosen ablations.

name: Evaluation and benchmarks
description: How recovered features are checked when the true features are unknown.

item.title: Measuring Progress in Dictionary Learning for Language Model Interpretability with Board Game Models
item.note: Chess and Othello models with known board properties as a test of dictionary recovery.

item.title: SAEBench: A Comprehensive Benchmark for Sparse Autoencoders in Language Model Interpretability
item.note: A benchmark across more than 200 dictionaries, seven architectures, and several metrics.

item.title: SynthSAEBench: Evaluating Sparse Autoencoders on Scalable Realistic Synthetic Data
item.note: Synthetic activations with hierarchy, correlations, and Zipfian firing, so recovered features can be checked against the truth.

item.title: Are Sparse Autoencoder Benchmarks Reliable?
item.note: Finds score differences between similar dictionaries within their own seed-to-seed variation.

item.title: Sanity Checks for Sparse Autoencoders: Do SAEs Beat Random Baselines?
item.note: Sparse autoencoders with directions kept at or near random initialization score close to trained ones on several evaluations.

item.title: Sparse but Wrong: Incorrect L₀ Leads to Incorrect Features in Sparse Autoencoders
item.note: Too low an L0 mixes correlated features, and too high an L0 admits degenerate mixtures.

item.title: Are Sparse Autoencoders Useful? A Case Study in Sparse Probing
item.note: Sparse-autoencoder probes against baselines under data scarcity, class imbalance, label noise, and covariate shift.

item.title: Decomposing the Dark Matter of Sparse Autoencoders
item.note: Models activations as sparse features plus a dense component, and studies the error that sparse autoencoders leave.

item.title: AxBench: Steering LLMs? Even Simple Baselines Outperform Sparse Autoencoders
item.note: Steering and concept detection across 500 concepts; dictionary methods are not competitive with simple baselines in its settings.

item.title: From Geometric Recovery to Causal Validation: A Reproducible Audit of Sparse Autoencoder Features
item.note: Ablates and steers recovered features in a synthetic setting to test whether they are causal.

name: Failure modes
description: Where recovered features differ from the network's features.

item.title: A is for Absorption: Studying Feature Splitting and Absorption in Sparse Autoencoders
item.note: Feature splitting and absorption: a specific latent takes over a general one when a child feature implies its parent.

item.title: Feature Hedging: Correlated Features Break Narrow Sparse Autoencoders
item.note: Dictionaries narrower than the feature set merge correlated features into one latent.

item.title: Sparse Autoencoders Do Not Find Canonical Units of Analysis
item.note: Latents at one dictionary width decompose into latents at another, so they are not canonical units.

item.title: Not All Language Model Features Are One-Dimensionally Linear
item.note: Days, months, and years lie on circles in two-dimensional subspaces.

item.title: When Models Manipulate Manifolds: The Geometry of a Counting Task
item.note: A counting task represented on a curved manifold that dictionary latents discretize.

item.title: Do Sparse Autoencoders Capture Concept Manifolds?
item.note: Separates capturing a concept manifold with a few latents from shattering or diluting it.

item.title: An Interpretability Illusion for BERT
item.note: Random directions show coherent top-activating examples about as often as neurons do.

item.title: Unstable Features, Reproducible Subspaces: Understanding Seed Dependence in Sparse Autoencoders
item.note: Estimates how likely a latent is to reappear in an independent training run.

item.title: Ablating Archetypes: The Stability of Archetypal SAEs is an Artifact of Initialization and Metric Design
item.note: Separates stable endpoints from convergence across independent runs for archetypal sparse autoencoders.

name: Applications and other domains
description: Steering, editing, and models beyond language.

item.title: Steering LLMs? Actually, Sparse Autoencoders Can Outperform Simple Baselines
item.note: With supervised labeling and selection, sparse-autoencoder steering approaches a LoRA reference while staying below prompting.

item.title: Look But Don't Touch with Sparse Autoencoders for Unlearning in Diffusion Models
item.note: Autoencoder-based concept erasure in diffusion models localizes the concept but often produces image artifacts.

item.title: Understanding Emergent Misalignment via Feature Superposition Geometry
item.note: Explains emergent misalignment by amplification of a target feature also amplifying overlapping directions.

item.title: Verbalizable Representations Form a Global Workspace in Language Models
item.note: Directions built from the model's sensitivity to its activations; a small share of a concept vector's variance carries much of its output effect.

item.title: Structuring Sparsity: Block-Sparse Featurizers Capture Visual Concept Manifolds
item.note: Vision concepts recovered as low-dimensional blocks rather than single directions, with generation steered within a block.

item.title: Superposition in Graph Neural Networks
item.note: Measures superposition in message-passing networks on synthetic graph tasks.

item.title: Sparse Autoencoders Reveal Organized Biological Knowledge but Minimal Regulatory Logic in Single-Cell Foundation Models
item.note: In a single-cell foundation model, only 3 of 48 transcription factors show target-specific latent responses under perturbation.

item.title: Mechanistic Interpretability of EEG Foundation Models via Sparse Autoencoders
item.note: Ranks dictionary latents by alignment with clinical concept directions in EEG foundation models.

item.title: Sparse Probes and Murky Physics: A Case Study of Interpretability Challenges in a Foundation Model for Continuum Dynamics
item.note: Recovered features in a fluid-dynamics emulator do not align with standard physical decompositions.

item.title: Superposition Is Not Necessary: A Mechanistic Interpretability Analysis of Transformer Representations for Time Series Forecasting
item.note: In a time-series forecaster, competitive forecasting does not require superposition.

name: Recent, not yet covered by the survey
description: Selected papers from July to October 2026.

item.title: High-probability guarantees for linear accessibility in feature superposition
item.note: For a fixed support with subgaussian noise, a linear readout needs a width of only about k log d with high probability.

item.title: Towards a mathematical theory of superposition
item.note: Recovery theorems for the tied readout ReLU(WᵀWx + b), built on frame theory and compressed sensing.

item.title: Emergent phases of superposition: from partial to full representation
item.note: Width drives a transition from representing a subset of the features to representing all of them.

item.title: The Ball and the Box: Two Geometries of Computation in Superposition
item.note: Sharp width thresholds for Boolean gates from a single threshold layer; the threshold depends on the error criterion.

item.title: Self-Confirming Superposition Traps in Reinforcement Learning
item.note: The reinforcement-learning loop can sustain a lower-return policy because optimal codes overlap features that rarely occur together.

item.title: Sparse Transformer: a Controlled Testbed for Mechanistic Interpretability
item.note: A small language model whose sparse MLP gives a reference basis for testing recovery methods.

item.title: Planning or Improvisation? Stress-Testing the Poetry Planning Site on Open Models and Open Cross-Layer Transcoders
item.note: Re-runs the rhyme-planning case study on open models with open cross-layer transcoders: position specificity generalizes, the planning site does not.
